summary: Captured incidentally during a Mode 2 sign attempt: console_wallet was invoked with --seed-words (Mode 2's seed), which triggered recovery against a fresh base-path. The wallet rescanned from height 0 to tip 670,998. Detected 1 UTXO of 30,000 tXTM (Mode 2's S0 funding had been received against this seed).

comparison_to_B0.interpretation: Recovery with 1 UTXO is 3.37x slower than empty-wallet scan. The extra cost is view-key matching against every block's outputs plus DB writes for the 1 detected output. Note this is a different code path (--recovery flag) from B0's daemon-mode scan; some of the difference may be code-path overhead rather than per-UTXO work.

caveats: Only 1 UTXO detected, not the spec's 512-UTXO pool. Extrapolating to 512 UTXOs assumes per-UTXO cost is constant which we have not verified.
Recovery code path differs from the daemon-mode scan that produced the B0 measurement. The 24,344 vs 82,000 blocks/sec gap may include code-path overhead, not just per-UTXO cost.
Did not capture peak RSS or peak CPU% during recovery.
what_would_make_this_a_real_S2: Recover console_wallet with the seed of the Mode 1 fresh wallet at port 18243 (which has ~470 UTXOs from S1 doubling+fanout). That wallet's seed words have not been extracted - console_wallet has no documented CLI command to dump them and TUI extraction is interactive.

Recommended upstream change: add `minotari_console_wallet show-seed-words --password ... --base-path ...` (mirrors the `show-seed-words` command minotari-cli already has) to enable scriptable seed extraction.
